sections.h2: Which Carroll County office do I call about a tax bill?
sections.html:
Call the Carroll County Tax Commissioner at 770-830-5843, or 770-830-5826 for the tag and tax counter. The office is at 423 College Street, Room 401, in Carrollton, and it is open 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM, Monday through Friday, with title work stopping at 4:30.

The commissioner's office prepares and mails the bills and collects the money, but it does not assess property or set millage rates. Those jobs belong to the Board of Tax Assessors, reached at 770-830-5812, and to the Board of County Commissioners and the Board of Education, which levy the rates. In Carroll County the assessors also take property tax returns and homestead applications.

  • Bill amount, late interest, returned mail: Tax Commissioner.
  • Value, exemptions, returns, appeals: Board of Tax Assessors.
  • Copy of your warranty deed: Clerk of Superior Court, in the Carroll County Courthouse.

The commissioner's website also takes online payments. A payment by card, in the office or online, carries a 2.5% service fee that goes to the payment processor, not to the county.

sections.h2: When are Carroll County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Generally December 1. The tax commissioner's FAQ explains that real estate and business personal property taxes were once due December 21, and that the county commissioners changed the date to December 1 by resolution in December 2009. Mobile and manufactured homes are due April 1, and vehicles are due by the owner's birthday.

Mailed payments are accepted on a United States Postal Service postmark, but not on a metered postmark. Tax bills go to the homeowner and never to the mortgage company, so a borrower with an escrow account has to pass the bill along.

After the due date, interest accrues monthly at the bank prime loan rate plus 3%. A 5% penalty applies to taxes still unpaid 120 days after the deadline, and another 5% is added every 120 days until it reaches 20%. Homesteaded property with a tax liability under $500 is excused from the penalty.

sections.h2: What does a lien do to a Carroll County sale?
sections.html:
When taxes stay unpaid more than 120 days after the due date, a tax FiFa can be recorded with the Clerk of Superior Court. That record is public, and the commissioner's office warns that credit bureaus can see it and use it. The office does not deal with the bureaus and cannot control how they treat the entry.

If the property taxes remain unpaid, the commissioner has the right and the duty to levy on the property. The office calls that a last resort and says it prefers other collection methods. The tax sales page of the commissioner's site lists the upcoming sale date, and states that bidders must bring cash, certified funds or a bank letter.

A sale of the house does not require you to wait for any of that. A title company can order a payoff figure from the commissioner, add it to the settlement statement and pay the county at closing, which clears the lien before a tax sale is ever scheduled.

sections.h2: How do I challenge a Carroll County assessment?
sections.html:
The annual notice of assessment must be mailed by July 1, and you have 45 days from the date on that notice to appeal in writing. Miss the date and the right to appeal for that year is lost. The notice states the fair market value, the assessed value and an estimate of tax based on last year's millage rates.

When you file, you pick one of three paths. The first is the County Board of Equalization, with a further appeal to Superior Court. The second is arbitration, with no appeal to Superior Court. The third is a hearing officer, available for non-homestead parcels with a fair market value above $1 million, with appeal rights to Superior Court.

  • Acceptable grounds are taxability, value, and uniformity with similar properties.
  • Complaints about the size of the tax levied are not grounds for an appeal.
  • Assessed value is 40% of fair market value, and the tax is the net assessed value times the millage rate.

sections.h2: Which Carroll County exemptions should a seller or buyer know about?
sections.html:
The Carroll County assessors accept homestead applications, and exemptions must be filed before April 1 to apply to that year. First-time applicants bring a copy of their warranty deed. After approval the exemption renews itself each year until the owner moves or the title changes.

Several programs sit on top of the standard exemption. The commissioner's general information page describes an elderly school tax exemption for owners 62 and older with net income at or below $10,000, a general exemption for owners 65 and older under the same income cap, and a deferral program for owners 62 and older with household income of $15,000 or less. The deferred tax stays on the property until ownership changes or it reaches 85% of fair market value, so a deferral comes due when the house is sold.

Agricultural land can qualify for assessment at 30% of fair market value, and conservation use land is valued at current use. Both require a covenant with the assessors to keep the qualifying use for at least 10 years. Ask the assessors what happens to the covenant before you sell acreage that carries one.

sections.h2: What is Carroll County like for someone selling a house?
sections.html:
Carroll County is in west Georgia on the Alabama line, covering about 499 square miles of land. Carrollton is the county seat and largest city, and Villa Rica, Temple, Bowdon, Mount Zion, Whitesburg and Roopville are the other municipalities. The eastern half of Villa Rica lies in Douglas County. Interstate 20 crosses the northern part, with U.S. 27, U.S. 78 and several state routes carrying local traffic.

The county was laid out in 1825 and was the site of Georgia's first gold rush. It is part of the Atlanta metro area, and the 2020 census counted 119,148 residents, with an estimate of 131,036 for 2025. Carroll has three school districts, and the Carrollton Greenbelt is among its walking and cycling routes. Tornadoes in February and May 2008 and flooding in September 2009 damaged homes and roads, so a buyer may ask about storm repairs on an older house.

faqs.q: What is the Carroll County property tax due date?
faqs.a: December 1 for real estate and business personal property, under a resolution the county commissioners adopted in December 2009. Mobile and manufactured homes are due April 1. Confirm the date on your own bill, since the commissioner's office mails it to the owner.

faqs.q: How much extra do I pay if I am late in Carroll County?
faqs.a: Interest builds monthly at the bank prime loan rate plus 3%, and a 5% penalty is added after 120 days, repeating every 120 days up to 20%. Homesteaded property with less than $500 in tax owed does not receive the penalty.

faqs.q: Can I pay Carroll County taxes by card?
faqs.a: Yes, in the office or online, and the payment processor adds a 2.5% service fee. The county does not collect that fee. Ask the tax commissioner which other ways to pay the office takes.

faqs.q: Does the Carroll County Tax Commissioner set my taxes?
faqs.a: No. The commissioner bills and collects based on the values from the Board of Assessors and the millage rates set by the county commissioners and the Board of Education. Questions about value go to the assessors at 770-830-5812.

faqs.q: When is the homestead filing deadline in Carroll County?
faqs.a: April 1. Applications received later take effect the next tax year. File with the Carroll County Tax Assessor's Office at 423 College Street, and bring a copy of your warranty deed if you are a first-time applicant.
